final_proof:
As stated, the claim is false: integrability alone does not ensure that the second derivative exists. For example, take \(a=-1\), \(b=1\), \(n=1\), and \(f(x)=|x|\). This function is continuous and hence integrable. Since \(h=2\), the trapezium approximation is
\[
T_1=\frac22\bigl(f(-1)+f(1)\bigr)=2,
\]
whereas
\[
I=\int_{-1}^{1}|x|\,dx=1.
\]
Thus \(T_1-I=1\). At every point where \(f''\) exists, it equals zero, while at \(x=0\) it does not exist. Hence no \(\xi\in[-1,1]\) satisfies the asserted formula.

The standard corrected theorem is as follows. Let \(a<b\), let \(n\ge1\), and suppose \(f\in C^2([a,b])\). Put
\[
h=\frac{b-a}{n},\qquad x_r=a+rh,
\]
and
\[
T_n=\frac h2\left(f(x_0)+f(x_n)+2\sum_{r=1}^{n-1}f(x_r)\right).
\]
Then there exists \(\xi\in[a,b]\) such that
\[
T_n-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx
 =\frac{(b-a)^3}{12n^2}f''(\xi).
\]

To prove this, fix \(r\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), write \(u=x_{r-1}\) and \(v=x_r\), and define
\[
w(x)=(x-u)(v-x).
\]
We have \(w(u)=w(v)=0\), \(w'(u)=h\), \(w'(v)=-h\), and \(w''=-2\). Two integrations by parts therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_u^v w(x)f''(x)\,dx
&=-\int_u^v w'(x)f'(x)\,dx\\
&=-[w'(x)f(x)]_u^v+\int_u^v w''(x)f(x)\,dx\\
&=h\bigl(f(u)+f(v)\bigr)-2\int_u^v f(x)\,dx.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac h2\bigl(f(u)+f(v)\bigr)-\int_u^v f(x)\,dx
 =\frac12\int_u^v(x-u)(v-x)f''(x)\,dx.
\]
Summing over all subintervals gives
\[
T_n-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\int_a^b K(x)f''(x)\,dx,
\]
where, for \(x\in[x_{r-1},x_r]\),
\[
K(x)=\frac12(x-x_{r-1})(x_r-x).
\]
The function \(K\) is continuous and nonnegative. Moreover, on each subinterval,
\[
\int_{x_{r-1}}^{x_r}K(x)\,dx
 =\frac12\int_0^h t(h-t)\,dt
 =\frac{h^3}{12}.
\]
Thus
\[
\int_a^bK(x)\,dx
 =\frac{nh^3}{12}
 =\frac{(b-a)^3}{12n^2}.
\]
Since \(f''\) is continuous and \(K\ge0\) has positive integral, the weighted mean value theorem gives some \(\xi\in[a,b]\) for which
\[
\int_a^bK(x)f''(x)\,dx
 =f''(\xi)\int_a^bK(x)\,dx.
\]
Combining the preceding identities proves the corrected formula.

If the error is instead defined as the exact integral minus the trapezium approximation, its sign is reversed. In either convention,
\[
\left|T_n-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\right|
\le \frac{(b-a)^3}{12n^2}\max_{x\in[a,b]}|f''(x)|.
\]
